data.narrative:
Ricursive Intelligence is a Series A-stage semiconductor company founded by Anna Goldie and Azalia Mirhoseini that has raised $335M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of eight private peers in chips and semiconductors at similar or adjacent stages, including Rebellions ($2.3B), d-Matrix ($2.0B), and Positron AI ($1.0B), alongside three public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Two methods proved applicable. The stage-progression approach, using total raised as a value proxy, applies a typical 2.0x Series A step-up multiplier to the $335M base, implying $670M. The peer-median method anchors to the $2.0B median valuation across the three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables, with a range of $1.0B to $2.3B. Public-comp anchoring was not applicable due to the absence of disclosed revenue figures for the target.

Triangulation across these two methods supports a valuation range of $570M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.3B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around the company's revenue trajectory, capital efficiency, and competitive positioning within the densely funded semiconductor infrastructure segment. The peer-median method carries greater weight given direct stage and sector alignment, though the stage-progression floor provides downside context.
